text:
maria: Quick heads up — during a canary rollout this morning a customer request fell back to a variant that had a different tokenizer and the tool-call JSON parsing failed. It surfaced as a 502 from the router. Anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking:

jason: yup saw that in staging at 07:32. The fallback model tokenizes a function name into two tokens, so the tool-caller regex doesn't match.

lee: oof. is this the same case where max_context also differs? I think the route remapped to a 4k model while the req used a 6k context window.

sophia: two issues here: tokenizer parity and context-length parity. For tool-calls we also need identical tool schema support (function signatures + arg types). If any of those differ we should mark the fallback as incompatible.

maria: Agreed. Proposal: extend the compatibility matrix to be explicit about tokenizer id, max_context, and tool_call_capability. Also add a router-level check that refuses fallback if any of the three are incompatible for customer-tier=enterprise?

jason: +1 for the matrix change. For routing, we need to be careful about tiers. Free/probation tiers should still be able to fall back to cheaper variants (best-effort), but enterprise/paid routes should be strict and failover to same-compat model or return 429 with graceful error.

lee: telemetry note: log an event "variant_mismatch" with fields: variant_from, variant_to, mismatch_reasons=["tokenizer","context","tool_schema"] and the request id. That will make it easy to query via kql.

ops-telemetry: infra-ticket created: INF-3219 to add variant_mismatch metric and a dashboard panel. ETA EOW.

maria: UX ask for Console rollout page: show a compatibility score per variant and a short explanation if a route will be prevented from falling back. Something like: "Fallback blocked: tokenizer mismatch (spm-v1 != spm-v2)". Also highlight which customers will be affected.

sophia: for the matrix format, suggest a compact JSON that the router can ingest at runtime. Example snippet below:

```json
{
  "variant_id": "gptx-v1-q8",
  "tokenizer": "spm-v2",
  "max_context": 8192,
  "tool_call_parity": true
}
```

maria: note: the above has double quotes — router config loader already expects JSON. We need the schema validated during model onboarding and also on any quantization pass that might change tokenizer behavior.

jason: small edgecase: some LLMs maintain identical tokenizer id but change token offsets (subtle detokenization differences). We should add a checksum (hash) of tokenizer merge table as a final guard.

lee: agree on checksum. Also for context-length, the router should check the incoming request's requested sequence length (or prompt length estimate) vs target's max_context and avoid fallback if unsafe.

maria: action items: 
1) eng-platform: add router rule to consult new compatibility matrix and a new flag for "strict_fallback" by customer tier. (owner: jason)
2) eng-ml: add tokenizer checksum and ensure onboarding pipeline emits tokenizer_id + checksum. (owner: sophia)
3) infra/telemetry: emit variant_mismatch events and dashboard tile. Link: INF-3219 (owner: ops-telemetry)
4) console: show compatibility warnings on rollout UI and per-route previews. (owner: lee)

jason: I'll open PR for router rule and add unit tests. Planning to include a small matrix loader and a fallback veto path.

sophia: will add checksum hook to onboarding and a CI gate that rejects variants that change tokenizer checksum without explicit acceptance.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled a canary run for router service tomorrow 03:00 UTC with new compatibility checks (dry-run). Will post logs in #eng-platform.

maria: thanks all. If we can get the telemetry early we can roll out the strict enforcement behind a feature flag and monitor for false positives. :thumbsup:
